status: Integrated into the local Sojourner cassette player on 2026-11-14.
processing: Source MP3 unchanged. Excerpts use 70 Hz high-pass, mild dynamics compression, measured two-pass loudness target -20 LUFS / -3 dBTP, 150ms fade-in, 250ms fade-out, mono 24 kHz 96 kbps MP3. No synthetic voice, added music, pitch or speed change. Existing source background music remains where present.
alignment: Cached local speech recognition plus NASA transcript used to identify speech boundaries. Source times refer to this supplied MP3, not mission elapsed time; speakers/wording follow NASA transcript rather than recognition guesses.
selection: Avoids harsh countdown/radio launch noise, computer-error ticking, zombie effects, and distressing/speculative death/abandonment narration. Brief celebratory cheers remain in first-wheels with reduced dynamic range. Child suitability remains an editorial judgement for owner review.

clips.title: Launch day
clips.description: Narrator gives the Pathfinder launch date. Harsh launch countdown and engine/radio noise omitted.

transcript.speaker: Narrator · 2022
transcript.text: The Pathfinder mission launched from Earth on December 4, 1996.

clips.title: First wheels on Mars
clips.kind: Modern narration followed by archival JPL mission-control audio
clips.description: Narrator explains overnight power saving and the ramp descent; original mission-control confirmation and brief cheers follow. Archive begins about 19.1 seconds into this excerpt.

transcript.speaker: Narrator · 2022
transcript.text: To save power, the lander and rover were programmed to go to sleep at night.

transcript.speaker: Narrator · 2022
transcript.text: When they woke up the next morning, the rover chatted with the lander like nothing had ever been wrong.

transcript.speaker: Narrator · 2022
transcript.text: With a sigh of relief, the team began directing the rover down the ramp so that it could finally touch Martian ground.

transcript.speaker: JPL Mission Control · 1997
transcript.text: We can report visually six wheels on soil.

clips.title: A team across space
clips.description: Dave Gruel explains rover/lander communications using a light-bulb comparison and describes the initial local link problem.

transcript.speaker: Dave Gruel · modern interview
transcript.text: The communications link between the lander and the rover was pretty basic.

transcript.speaker: Dave Gruel · modern interview
transcript.text: You know, we think about the fact that we can communicate with a vehicle that’s on the surface of Mars, that’s millions of miles away, and the power that it gives off is similar to the power of a light bulb in your refrigerator.

transcript.speaker: Dave Gruel · modern interview
transcript.text: And we can make out those ones and zeros here on Earth and figure out what that says about the surface of another planet, yet we couldn’t get these two vehicles, who are in close proximity to one another, to communicate well.

clips.title: A lasting adventure
clips.description: Narrator summarizes the missions exceeding their intended lifetimes and their lasting influence. No speculative final-rover story or later-mission claims included.

transcript.speaker: Narrator · 2022
transcript.text: Sojourner and Pathfinder may only have been active a few short months, but they lasted many times longer than designed, and their influence continues to this day.

transcript.speaker: Narrator · 2022
transcript.text: They changed how we explore Mars, and marked the start of 25 years of Mars rover adventures.
